name: Engine turning
summary: A lathe with a cutting tool cuts a regular pattern of fine lines in a flat metal face. The pattern catches the light and shows no tool marks.
how: Fix the metal blank on the rose engine, and set the cam that gives the pattern.
Cut each line at a depth of 0.05 to 0.1 mm, and keep the pitch the same.
Polish the cut lines, or fill them with clear enamel.

origin.note: Craftsmen cut patterns on a rose engine lathe in wood, ivory and soft metal.

adoptions.via: Breguet cuts engine-turned patterns of lines and waves in the gold or silver dial of a watch.
Deco watch dials of silver and gold carry engine-turned patterns, sometimes under clear enamel.
The dial of the Royal Oak carries a grid pattern in the manner of engine turning, called the tapisserie.
